title: The lanes hook sometimes runs past its 10 s limit
what: Find what the lanes hook waits on in a slow run (time each git and file step, log runs over 2 s with the step), bound the hook's own work well under the limit (each git call with a timeout; on overrun print one short line that the lanes are not known this time, never block), and keep the 10 s limit in hooks.json.
why: 29 Oct, twice in the owner's session (about 14:45 and 15:20 local) Claude Code showed the owner 'UserPromptSubmit hook [python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lanes.py] timed out after 10s — output discarded. Raise the hook's "timeout" to allow more time.' The owner asked twice what it means. Measured right after, at load 48 on 12 cores: 0.7-0.9 s per run (3 runs), so the slow runs are rare and the cause is not known (a git lock held by a landing or a gate commit, swap while the podman machine held 20 GB, or a slow git call). A hook that runs at every owner message must never block it, and a warning that names an internal file tells the owner nothing (principle 10).
failing_case: On a loaded machine, during a landing or a gate commit, the UserPromptSubmit lanes hook takes over 10 s and Claude Code shows the owner the timeout warning.
pass_cases: a lanes hook run whose git call blocks (a test holding the index lock or a fake slow git) returns within 5 s with one line that the lanes are unknown
a normal run prints the same lanes line as today
a run over 2 s leaves a log line naming the slow step
